Hi all — I pulled the ledger and did an initial cross-check against the CSV QueueBack attached. Summary below (high level):

What we found
- The rows in your CSV map to three distinct request ids in our telemetry cluster. Two of the request ids were tagged as "env:staging" at ingestion, one was tagged as "env:prod".
- Our billing ledger uses a mid-cycle proration algorithm when a customer crosses rate bands (see: hourly bucket attribution -> prorate to usage timestamp). For Oct 14-17 the customer crossed from the PAYG band to Tier 2 on Oct 15 03:40 UTC — the system prorated token prices for requests that spanned the boundary.
- We also applied our prefix-caching reduction (prefix cache hits are excluded from token billing) — the CSV shows a high number of cached generation retries that were not charged. The net effect should reduce billed tokens, not increase them.

Root cause hypothesis
- The 38k token delta appears to be primarily caused by: 1) two requests incorrectly ingested without the staging tag (so they were billed at production rates), and 2) proration window rounding that shifted ~8k tokens into the higher-priced bucket when usage straddled the Oct 15 rate boundary.

Preliminary numbers (provisional)
- Raw token delta reported by QueueBack: 38,120 tokens
- Tokens billed to Ledger (Oct 14-17): 112,340 tokens
- Tokens we now believe should have been billed (corrected): 74,210 tokens
- Provisional net credit (USD): $1,062.48 (VAT handling TBD)

Attachments included: provisional_credit_calculation.xlsx (breakdown by request id + per-token pricing)

Immediate remediation options
1) We can issue a provisional credit for the net difference and apply it to INV-202710-0421.
2) We can backfill a ledger correction and reissue an updated invoice and credit note (preferred if you need a formal accounting trail).

VAT note
- Because QueueBack is an EU-registered company and you appear to have an EU VAT ID on file, we need to confirm whether you want the credit issued with reverse-charge (zero VAT) or as a VAT-bearing credit. Our accounting needs either a VAT-exempt confirmation (reverse-charge proof) or we will include VAT on the adjustment.

I’ll wait for confirmation from QueueBack on (a) whether you want the provisional credit applied now and (b) VAT preference. If you want the formal reissue path, we’ll start the backfill and flag this as a retroactive ledger correction (that takes 3–5 business days).
